scope: Part A — the three Stage 1 defects, plus the opt-in NF4 load path the approved quantization policy requires. Nothing else in the production paths was modified.

defects.title: Qwen3 thinking-mode constructor override
defects.severity: medium (produced a false result in Stage 1)
defects.observed: HFLocalChatLLM.__init__ applied chat_template_kwargs.update(_maybe_thinking_kwargs(model_id)), and that helper returns {'enable_thinking': False} for every Qwen3-family model. An explicitly requested enable_thinking=True was overwritten at construction, so the Mode A/Mode B judge comparison initially compared thinking-off against itself.
defects.root_cause: dict.update() treats a computed model-family default as if it were an explicit override.

fix.current_behavior: family default overwrote an explicit enable_thinking
fix.required_change: apply the family default with setdefault() so explicit configuration wins: precedence is explicit value > model-family default
fix.experimental_risk: none — the production judge still defaults to thinking off

non_goals: judge prompts, rubric, scoring and parser untouched
enable_thinking default for Qwen3-family models unchanged (still False)

defects.title: release_pipeline / lingering model reference
defects.severity: high (presented as an opaque CUDA OOM)
defects.observed: HFLocalChatLLM._pipeline was a second strong reference alongside the module-level _pipeline_cache, so release_pipeline() removed the cache entry and freed nothing. Measured in Stage 1: cache dropped only, ~15 GiB still allocated; client reference + cache dropped, ~0.008 GiB.
defects.root_cause: Two owners for one allocation, with no enforcement that a caller drops the second one.

fix.current_behavior: client held a strong reference; release needed two steps
fix.required_change: the cache becomes the sole strong owner; the client's handle is a weakref, and the loader keeps a strong local handle only until the cache takes ownership (otherwise the pipeline could be collected between creation and caching)
fix.experimental_risk: low — a released model is reloaded on next use, which is the pre-existing contract; a live generation keeps its own reference, so release during generation cannot pull weights out from under a call
fix.performance_impact: none; release is what it always claimed to be

non_goals: VRAM safety gates unchanged (pre-load, post-load, per-run floor, ceiling)
residency ceiling not raised; no CPU offload
no ad-hoc empty_cache() calls scattered through the attack code
no change to which models the experiment keeps resident

defects.title: judge JSON failure indistinguishable from score 1
defects.observed: llm_evaluate_with_rubric returned 1 whenever the evaluator reply was not a dict carrying a score in 1..5. Score 1 is also the rubric's genuine refusal verdict, so an evaluator failure was recorded as a safe verdict.
defects.root_cause: Two distinct outcomes (valid score 1, unusable output) collapsed onto one return value.

fix.required_change: classify each reply (VALID / EMPTY_OUTPUT / JSON_PARSE_ERROR / MISSING_SCORE / INVALID_SCORE_TYPE / SCORE_OUT_OF_RANGE), record it in an append-only telemetry log, and return None for anything but a valid score — never a substituted 1
fix.experimental_risk: a failed evaluation now propagates as None into the attack's score list (Turn.judge_score is already int|None); the attack text that quotes the last score therefore shows 'None' on the rare failure path

non_goals: no rubric text change, no score-meaning change
no retries, no JSON repair, no regex extraction, no fallback scoring
valid scores keep their exact semantics (score 1 remains 1)
judge model, revision and thinking mode untouched

defects.title: opt-in NF4 load path (required by the approved quantization policy)
defects.observed: The frozen attacker interface (HFLocalChatLLM) had no way to express the approved 4-bit NF4 PTQ load, so the approved configuration could not be driven through the interface it is meant to be qualified against.

fix.required_change: add an opt-in quantization='nf4' load path; default None leaves the path unchanged
fix.experimental_risk: any experiment that sets quantization='nf4' runs 4-bit weights; no existing config sets it, so frozen runs are unaffected
fix.validation: TestQuantizationIsOptIn (4 tests) asserting the default carries no quantization kwargs

non_goals: no change to generation parameters, prompts, parsers or NBF
